content.text: Manually curated official-source snapshot retrieved 22 October 2026 from the Registrar General's Department pages on obtaining certified copies and on charges; not independently validated, not live output, and not an official application service. Scope: the counter application for a certified copy of a birth certificate through a Divisional Secretariat. The separate online eBMD application, with its own payment instructions, is a different channel and is not covered. An older Government Information Centre page lists Rs. 100 and Rs. 200 for the same two cases; the Registrar General's Department figures of Rs. 120 and Rs. 250 are used. Verify current requirements with the department.
Get the application form from the Registrar Division of any Divisional Secretariat, or download it from the Registrar General's Department website.
Complete the application for the Divisional Secretariat of the place of birth, giving the birth certificate number and registration date if you know them, because this decides which charge applies.

If the birth certificate number and registration date are known, pay Rs. 120 per copy at the Divisional Secretariat or at the Registrar General's Bank of Ceylon branch at Battaramulla, and keep the bank slip. Payments by ATM or online are not accepted.

Submit the completed application with the bank slip to the Divisional Secretariat of the place of birth. For delivery by post, enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope. If the birth is registered you receive as many copies as you paid for; if it is not registered you are notified on Form B38.

If the number or date is not known and a search of the records for up to two years is needed, pay Rs. 250 for the first copy and Rs. 120 for each additional copy at the Divisional Secretariat or at the Registrar General's Bank of Ceylon branch at Battaramulla, and keep the bank slip. Payments by ATM or online are not accepted.

Submit the completed application with the bank slip to the Divisional Secretariat of the place of birth. For delivery by post, enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope. If the birth is registered you receive as many copies as you paid for; if it is not registered you are notified on Form B38.
